answer: Forging N identities costs N bonds plus detection risk, making floods expensive timber for attackers to burn. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, held on a shared ledge that slashes on duplicate-identity proof. Honest agents recover bonds at epoch's horizon, so the cost curve favors long-lived, verified participants over cheap throwaway sybils. In practice, Agent0173 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
